legend: Tubular carcinoma accompanied by precursor lesions – lobular carcinoma in situ (left) and low-grade ductal carcinoma in situ (right).
Tubular carcinoma at low magnification. Haphazard distribution of round and angulated tubules with open lumina, embedded in abundant desmoplastic stroma.
Core needle biopsy showing haphazardly arranged tubules.
p63 immunohistochemistry highlights the absence of myoepithelial cells around the malignant tubules, in contrast to the normal tubules (arrows).
ER immunohistochemistry showing strong and diffuse nuclear staining in the tumour cells.
Tubular carcinoma with prominent apical snouts (arrow).
Ultrasound shows a hypoechoic irregular mass.

legend: Core biopsy shows an invasive carcinoma with tubular features, comprising patent and angulated tubules lined by mostly single layered cuboidal cells with apical snouts, disposed within desmoplastic stroma. Accompanying changes of columnar cell hyperplasia, atypical ductal hyperplasia and low grade DCIS are present. Scattered calcifications are seen.
Tubular carcinoma associated with precursor lesions - LCIS and low-grade DCIS

diagnosis: Invasive carcinoma with tubular features, provisional grade 1
legend: Vacuum assisted breast biopsy shows haphazardly distributed angulated tubules lined by epithelial cells with mild to moderate nuclear pleomorphism and rare mitosis, consistent with an invasive carcinoma with tubular features.  Non-neoplastic breast tissue shows fibrocystic and columnar cell changes. Immunohistochemistry for ER and PR is diffusely positive in invasive carcinoma cells, while SMMHC shows lack of a peripheral rim of myeopithelial cells around invasive carcinoma.

Tubular structures, many angulated, within fibroblastic stroma. Tubules are lined by a single layer of moderately atypical malignant epithelial cells. By definition, tubular carcinoma is of histological grade 1 (as here, 121).
